title: Choosing the Right Fitting for Horizontal Drain Transitions
description: Installing horizontal drainage lines requires careful selection of directional fittings to maintain waste velocity and prevent blockages. Standard sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions, not horizontal-to-horizontal branch connections. When joining horizontal drain lines, using a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye directs waste smoothly into the main channel. This reduces flow turbulence, minimizes splash back, and prevents waste from accumulating at the branch junction.

Standard sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal transitions, not horizontal-to-horizontal branch connections. When joining horizontal drain lines, using a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye directs waste smoothly into the main channel. This reduces flow turbulence, minimizes splash back, and prevents waste from accumulating at the branch junction.
